A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Equivariant Neural Fields work, with matching core definitions and experiments. Text, equations, tables, figures and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison despite substantial revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original image reconstruction, CIFAR10 classification and ShapeNet experiments, plus qualitative latent editing and clustering results in the main text and Appendix A.

after.justification: v4 reports original reconstruction, classification, segmentation and forecasting experiments, with additional robustness tests and appendix ablations.

M1.justification: The bi-invariant cross-attention and FiLM backbone remains, but v4 introduces attention restricted to each coordinate's k nearest latents. It also specifies new downstream procedures: a second ENF for segmentation and a latent-update PONITA model for forecasting, including a reconstruction-error-aware forecasting objective (Section 4.2 and Appendix C.1). These substantially extend the implemented procedure.

E1.justification: CIFAR10 and CelebA remain, while STL10 disappears and ImageNet1K is added. The earlier 10-class ShapeNet study becomes 16-class occupancy/classification/part-segmentation and 55-class SDF evaluations. New domains include multimodal OMBRIA flood mapping and ERA5 temperature forecasting, with missing-observation and changed-resolution test scenarios.

E2.justification: v4 adds reported comparisons with PointNet, PointNet++, DGCNN and NF2vec for shape segmentation, OmbriaNet for flood mapping, and an identity forecasting reference. Functa remains. The earlier ENF-abs-rel-pos/norm-rel-pos variant disappears from image comparisons, while translation and PONITA roto-translation variants remain under new names. The non-equivariant control changes from absolute coordinates x to concatenated pose and coordinate inputs.

E3.justification: Reported CIFAR10 latent configurations change from 16 points of dimension 32 to 25 of dimension 64; CelebA changes from 25 of dimension 128 to 36 of dimension 64. The downstream classifier changes from four layers using rotational invariants to three layers using attributes matched to the ENF. Added experiments introduce segmentation-specific evaluation, one-hour forecasting, observation subsampling and zero-shot resolution-transfer protocols.

E4.justification: v4 adds a roughly fixed-parameter latent-count/context-dimension ablation (Appendix D.1), a shape-segmentation control using only object class (D.2), and OMBRIA sparsity and resolution-transfer tests. Conversely, v1's shape stitching and appendix CelebA clustering, latent mixing and interpolation demonstrations are removed. Transformation and car–duck stitching demonstrations remain.

E5.justification: Neither version reports experimental seeds, repeated-run counts, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. The additional class/instance averages and random sampling descriptions in v4 do not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Image reconstruction values change: translation-equivariant CIFAR10 PSNR is 34.8 in v1 Table 1 and 42.2 in v4 Table 1 under revised model settings, while its classification accuracy remains 82.1%. Shape results are replaced by different class/modality settings. Substantial new results include segmentation, robustness, ablation and forecasting outcomes, such as OMBRIA full-observation IoU of 74.00 and ERA5 forecast MSE of 9.44e-06.

T1.justification: The steerability/bi-invariance lemma and its proof are retained. The written Gaussian-window definition changes from a positive squared-distance term in v1 Section 3.4 to a negative squared-distance bias using positional pose components in v4 Section 3.1. This is a limited mathematical revision.

C1.justification: The central steerability, locality and weight-sharing claims remain. However, the abstract and contributions expand claimed validation from reconstruction, classification and editing to fine-grained segmentation, forecasting and super-resolution/resolution transfer. The asserted applicability and downstream benefits therefore become substantially broader.

C2.justification: v4 adds substantive qualifications about attention cost versus locality, insufficient shape reconstruction through meta-learning, and limited equivariance gains on aligned ShapeNet objects. Its class-only segmentation control supports a new interpretation involving positional shortcuts. It also discusses Functa overfitting on OMBRIA, initialization sensitivity and tentative parameter-efficiency benefits, extending v1's mainly general explanations of geometric representations.

D1.justification: Compared with v1's sparse experimental specifications, v4 Appendices A–C provide initialization guidance, autodecoding pseudocode, optimizer and learning-rate settings, RFF bandwidths, architecture sizes, training budgets, preprocessing and H100 hardware information. Section 6 and embedded links add implementation and data-access information, reporting partial experimental code availability while promising the remaining code.

R1.justification: The principal lineage through Functa, cross-attention neural fields and PONITA remains. v4 adds Spatial Functa as context for global-latent limitations and neural ideograms/Kendall shape VAEs as inspiration, while dropping the earlier Field2Vec/metanetwork motivation. Additional neural-field and dataset references broaden the context without fundamentally changing the method's positioning.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and background are extensively rewritten. Encoding background and meta-learning pseudocode move into an expanded appendix; the method is reorganized into architecture and latent acquisition, and experiments are reorganized around reconstruction and downstream tasks. A reproducibility section and structured technical appendices replace the earlier brief experimental appendix.

P2.justification: v4 substantially redesigns the introductory and method schematics, adds a locality illustration, combines image reconstruction/classification into one table, and introduces segmentation and forecasting displays. Several earlier editing figures disappear, while retained transformation and stitching examples receive revised panels or annotations. Table arrangements, captions, typography and page layout also change substantially.

improvement.justification: v4 resolves important evidential weaknesses: v1 Table 3 juxtaposes ENF SDF reconstruction with Functa voxel reconstruction, whereas v4 Table 2 compares both methods within each representation. New fine-grained tasks, robustness tests and the ShapeNet shortcut control substantially strengthen evaluation, while detailed appendices improve reproducibility. Some editing evidence is lost and reporting errors remain, including the CIFAR10 sentence using 68.7 where Table 1 gives Functa 68.3. Nevertheless, the stronger comparison design and technical documentation establish a substantial overall improvement.
